data.name: Hajun
data.gender_notes: Hajun is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Originating from the Arabic root 'hajj' meaning 'to journey' or 'to go', Hajun is a unisex name that symbolizes strength, power, and courage. In Arabic, Hajun means 'mountain'. The name Hajun carries the meaning “Mountain” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Hajun usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes one's journey towards spiritual growth and enlightenment, much like the arduous climb up a mountain.
data.etymology: Hajun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mountain.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hajun total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hindi.name: औलय

in_pashto.name: علي
in_pashto.long_meaning: Although 'Ali' is not a common Pashtun name, it is transliterated in the same way as in Arabic and Urdu. Its meaning in Pashto is 'Shahrzad', the legendary heroine from the One Thousand and One Nights tale.

data.cultural_impact: In the Islamic world, the Hajj pilgrimage is considered one of the most important religious journeys a Muslim can make. Hajun as a name can evoke the spirit of this significant pilgrimage, symbolizing the idea of embarking on a life-changing journey to seek spiritual enlightenment and grow closer to God. It also highlights the importance of leaving behind comforts, worldly possessions, and distractions to focus on the essential.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Hajun represents not just a physical journey but a journey of the soul towards self-discovery, growth, and ultimately, union with the divine. The name serves as a constant reminder of the significance of making the effort to connect with God, overcoming obstacles and inner struggles, and striving for spiritual development. It's a reminder that life's greatest rewards come from the journey, not the destination.
